fix: land the review fixes that were pushed after their PRs merged (#108)

* fix: land the review fixes that were pushed after their PRs merged

Five commits were pushed to PR branches after the PR had already merged, so
they never reached main. Three of them fixed things already reported as done.

- gitleaks: allowlist the Python tool caches on generic-api-key, the form
  8.24.3 honours (a top-level block is ignored there; a scanner-level one is
  rejected by newer versions next to [[allowlists]])
- web: the vendor-chunk check looks at every package, keeps its own list, and
  validates its own table
- manage.sh: report a failed backup on stderr, which is what POST /api/backup
  returns; with a Bats test that fails against the old script
- ruff: drop the exclude list that replaced ruff's 25 defaults with 7

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(backup): report every failure on stderr, and show the API's reason in the panel

Review of #108. create_backup still wrote two of its three failure messages to
stdout (no data directory; failed integrity check), which POST /api/backup never
returns, and left an unreadable archive in backups/. useErrorHandler preferred
err.message, which an Axios error always has, over the reason the API returned,
so the panel showed 'Request failed with status code 500'.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: make the unreadable-archive fixture fail on GNU tar too

GNU tar lists a junk stream shorter than one 512-byte block as an empty archive
and exits 0; BSD tar rejects it. The fixture is now 1024 bytes, which both
reject. Checked on macOS and on ubuntu 24.04 with Bats 1.10.

commits.message:
chore(ci): CI_SERIAL=1 runs the BATS suite after the fast checks, as before

Serial mode ran the suite first, so it delayed finding an early lint failure
and did not match the order the docs describe.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

chore(web): upgrade to Vite 8 and plugin-react 6, and check the vendor chunks (#103)

Vite 8 bundles with Rolldown, which rejects the object form of
manualChunks; the vendor split now uses codeSplitting groups. A lost group
would not fail the build, so check-build-chunks.mjs asserts the chunks and
runs in CI and make ci (which never ran the web build before).

Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(scripts): cleanup-system.sh no longer deletes backups, wipes /tmp, or prunes unused volumes (#97)

- backups are left to cleanup-backups.sh (run by backup-scheduler.sh after every
  backup, retention-aware); the old step deleted every *.tar.gz older than 30 days
  once there were more than 10, which could leave one and took the *.deleted.*
  safety backups world-manager.sh writes
- no more rm -rf /tmp/* or ~/.cache/*: only the pip cache is removed
- docker: prune dangling images and week-old build cache instead of
  `system prune -af --volumes`; report "cleaned with warnings" when a prune fails
- new BATS suite; rm and sudo are stubbed so a regression cannot touch the
  machine running the tests

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
refactor(api): split the permission model and request authentication out of server.py (#93)

- api/rbac.py: permission names, role table, API-key scoping (pure data/functions)
- api/auth_guard.py: require_auth, require_permission, has_permission, CSRF checks,
  get_username_from_request; reads USERS/API_KEYS from api.server at call time
- blueprints, server.py and test patch targets use the new modules directly
- delete the unused require_api_key decorator
- auth_guard imports server after its own definitions, so importing it first no
  longer fails with a partially initialised module; test_import_order.py covers it
- issue_csrf_token is public (used across modules); /api/status no longer stacks
  require_auth on require_permission
- document that an unknown and a disabled API key get the same response, with a test
- AGENTS.md: endpoint convention now matches how blueprints are written

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

chore(web): bump Playwright to 1.63.0 and pin it with its CI image (#100)

* chore(web): bump Playwright to 1.63.0 and pin it with its CI image

@playwright/test and playwright are pinned exactly in package.json (the version must
equal the CI container's tag), the lockfile, PLAYWRIGHT_IMAGE in the Makefile and the
playwright-tests job's image and version guard move to 1.63.0. All 17 browser tests
pass in the 1.63.0 image against the existing screenshot baselines, so none were
re-rendered. docs/CI_CD.md lists the four places to change together, since Renovate
bumps the npm packages but not the image tag.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: make the Playwright version check read the pins instead of repeating one

Copilot review: the playwright-tests job's first step compared the lockfile with a
second hard-coded "1.63.0", so updating the container image alone could still pass.
A job's container image has to be a literal, so the check now reads it.

scripts/check-playwright-pin.sh takes the lockfile as the source of truth and checks
package.json (pinned exactly), the Makefile's PLAYWRIGHT_IMAGE and the workflow's
container image against it, requires exactly one image tag in each file, and reports
every disagreement. The workflow step runs it, so does `make ci`, and it has BATS
tests (the image or the lockfile updated alone, a caret range, two images, an
unreadable lockfile; they fail with the workflow comparison removed).

Also drop the hard-coded test count from the changelog (AGENTS.md: no counts in prose).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(api): split config redaction, path validation and auth crypto out of server.py (#92)

- api/config_redaction.py: redact_config_secrets, describe_yaml_error
- api/paths.py: _within_allowed_roots, is_path_allowed, resolve_allowed_path
- api/auth_crypto.py: password hashing, JWT, TOTP, Apple ID-token verification
- callers and test patch targets use the new modules directly; no re-exports
- state the tests patch (PROJECT_ROOT, ALLOWED_FILE_PATHS, SECRET_KEY) stays
  on api.server and is read at call time
- CodeQL totals unchanged (37: 32 error, 2 warning, 3 note)

Two small behaviour fixes found while moving the code:
- bcrypt and PyJWT shared one try/except, so a missing bcrypt also disabled
  JWTs and Apple sign-in; pyotp and qrcode did the same, which would have
  blocked 2FA logins when only qrcode (setup QR image) was missing. Each is
  now imported separately; TOTP_AVAILABLE becomes PYOTP_AVAILABLE and
  QRCODE_AVAILABLE.
- tests for the invalid-YAML error responses, which had none.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

chore(api): replace eventlet with Flask-SocketIO threading mode (#90)

- async_mode="threading" with simple-websocket; no monkey-patching
- drop eventlet from requirements, add simple-websocket
- socketio.run passes allow_unsafe_werkzeug=True (single process behind nginx)
- update roadmap O7, changelog, and the stale eventlet notes in docs/systemd

Verified against a live server over polling and WebSocket transports.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
test(scripts): add BATS suites for world-manager.sh and plugin-manager.sh, and fix what they found (#95)

world-manager.sh
- per-world config now applies: it was source'd, and the CREATED line (a date
  with a space) made every source fail, so config never worked and switch died
  after editing level-name; the config is read as plain data and never executed
- config/switch on a world with no config file no longer go through create,
  which offered to overwrite the world and moved it aside on yes
- delete no longer removes a world whose backup could not be written
- values written into server.properties are escaped for sed; the seed is
  appended with printf; create refuses control characters in type and seed
- names like ../x are refused; the tar fallback for templates (no rsync) puts
  --exclude before the path so player data stays out
- any directory under data/ with a level.dat is a world, not only world*
  (backups create leaves beside a world are skipped)

plugin-manager.sh
- depend: [A, B] and block-list dependencies are understood
- a jar's declared name is not trusted as a path; names given to
  enable/disable/remove/update that point outside plugins/ are refused
- the config backup no longer leaves an empty directory; a failed unzip no
  longer leaks a temp dir

Both suites also pass on Ubuntu (GNU userland).

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(mobile): stop closed nav menu from blocking taps (#113)

A mobile "GPU acceleration" rule set `.nav-menu { transform:
translateZ(0) }`, overriding the closed menu's translateX(-100%). The
menu sat invisibly (opacity 0) over the whole viewport and caught every
tap below the navbar. Drop .nav-menu from that rule and hide the closed
menu with visibility so its links also leave the tab order.

Adds an e2e regression test for the mobile menu.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
